summary: Repaired /srv/inventory permissions on node1 (created inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, set ownership and 750/640 modes so only inventorysvc/group members can access it, others get nothing), preserving all existing data. Verified access control with temporary test users (reader in group could read, outsider was denied), then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, confirmed the boot_id changed after reconnecting, and reverified ownership, permissions, and full data contents post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory contents and ownership on node1
Created system group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc (primary group inventory-readers)
chmod 750 on all directories and 640 on all files under /srv/inventory
Verified data files (records.csv, config.json) contents unchanged
Created temporary test users to confirm group members can read and non-members are denied, then cleaned them up
Captured pre-restart boot_id and confirmed data/permissions healthy
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 (backgrounded so ack returned)
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified user/group existence, permissions, and data integrity post-restart

evidence.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory is preserved (owner/group/content unchanged in substance)
evidence.summary: Initial listing showed root-owned files with world-readable content; after chown/chmod the same records.csv and config.json content was printed unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Ownership set to inventorysvc, group set to inventory-readers
evidence.summary: ls -ld output shows all files/dirs under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers.

evidence.requirement: Readable by inventory-readers group, inaccessible to other users
evidence.summary: A test user added to inventory-readers could cat records.csv; a test user outside the group got Permission denied. Mode 750/640 confirmed with no rwx bits for others. Test users were removed afterward.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 67f3a44b-85c6-40fe-8529-fcb6e8ac337a plus confirmed permissions and data readability by inventorysvc before reboot.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot was backgrounded with nohup; the exec call returned 'reboot command issued' successfully before the node went down.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: proof node actually went down and came back with changed boot identity
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node offline mid-reboot); second poll returned boot_id 997b9f75-c2ff-4cde-8abd-5c44b3b2b0e9, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: post-restart recovery of required state
evidence.summary: After reboot, inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group still exist, /srv/inventory retains 750/640 ownership and permissions, and both data files are intact and readable by inventorysvc.
